newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco stocks surge on report of talks.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco stocks surge on report of talks.

text.p: The stocks of tobacco companies surged on Wednesday in response to a published report that tobacco companies had started negotiating a possible settlement of pending litigation.

The report, published in the Wednesday edition of the Wall Street Journal, said the nation's two largest cigarette makers, Philip Morris Cos. and RJR Nabisco Holding Corp., were in secret talks with plaintiffs on what would be a sweeping settlement.

A possible agreement would cover the tobacco industry's liability for smoking in return for advertising curbs and a payment that could total $300 billion over the next 25 years, the report said. The Journal story said it was quoting people familiar with the situation.
In early trading on the New York Stock Exchange, Philip Morris traded at $40.875 a share, up $2, and RJR Nabisco was unchanged at $30.25 after adding $1 in pre-opening trading.

B.A.T Industries, holding company for Brown & Williamson, the No. 3 maker of cigarettes in the United States, was trading at 523 pence a share, up from 513 pence Tuesday, on the London Stock Exchange.
An RJR Nabisco official declined to comment on the report, but said the company would listen to "any reasonable proposals" aimed at ending face-offs with anti-tobacco forces.

The official, Charles Blixt, general counsel for the Reynolds Tobacco unit of RJR Nabisco, made the statement in response to a question prior to the start of RJR Nabisco's annual shareholders meeting in Winston-Salem, N.C.
